recommendations.claim: High-dose fish oil (EPA/DHA ~3-4 g/day) may modestly support muscle-recovery markers, but the human-outcome evidence for recovery specifically is trial-stage and mixed; its established human-outcome evidence is in the triglyceride/cardiovascular domain.
recommendations.source: EFSA NDA opinion on supplemental long-chain n-3 (combined EPA+DHA up to ~5 g/day no safety concern, general population); muscle-recovery/DOMS RCT literature is small and heterogeneous (trial-stage); triglyceride-lowering meta-analyses are the established-rung human-outcome anchor.
recommendations.confidence_tier: maturity_rung: established for triglyceride/CV outcomes, trial-stage for recovery; GRADE certainty low-to-moderate (recovery), strength conditional
recommendations.reversibility: Fully reversible; effects and antiplatelet contribution resolve within days-to-weeks of discontinuation.

interactions.mechanism: concurrent perturbation of the hemostatic/vascular axis — high-dose fish oil contributes a documented antiplatelet/bleeding-risk effect while BPC-157 is angiogenic/vascular-acting with a thrombotic worst-case and near-zero human-outcome data; the net hemostatic interaction is uncharacterized in humans
